776.08.title: Forcible felony.

rows.trigger: Purely definitional. The entire section is one undesignated sentence with no subsections, no paragraphs, and no subparagraphs. It defines the term "forcible felony" for use elsewhere in the Florida Statutes and assigns NO degree of offense, NO penalty, and NO term of imprisonment to anything. Degrees for the enumerated crimes are assigned by their own separate statutes (e.g. murder, robbery, burglary, arson), not by 776.08. Two structural features an auditor must note: (1) the list is closed-ended only in part -- it ends with a residual catch-all clause, "any other felony which involves the use or threat of physical force or violence against any individual," so the enumerated list is NOT exhaustive; (2) several enumerated terms (burglary, aggravated assault, robbery) are themselves defined elsewhere and their inclusion here is unqualified on the face of this section, i.e. this section states no exception for non-violent variants of those offenses. No dollar values, no value ladder, no prior-conviction enhancement, and no place-based or item-based narrowing appear anywhere in this section.
rows.quote: “Forcible felony” means treason; murder; manslaughter; sexual battery; carjacking; home-invasion robbery; robbery; burglary; arson; kidnapping; aggravated assault; aggravated battery; aggravated stalking; aircraft piracy; unlawful throwing, placing, or discharging of a destructive device or bomb; and any other felony which involves the use or threat of physical force or violence against any individual.

775.084.title: Violent career criminals; habitual felony offenders and habitual violent felony offenders; three-time violent felony offenders; definitions; procedure; enhanced penalties or mandatory minimum prison terms.

rows.trigger: Habitual felony offender whose current offense is a life felony or first degree felony. This section assigns NO degree of offense at all -- it prescribes a term directly for an already-graded felony. There is no dollar value anywhere in s. 775.084, so min and max are null for every row, not merely unstated. Eligibility requires the (1)(a) findings: two or more prior felony convictions or qualified offenses, the new felony committed while serving a sentence/supervision for a prior felony or within 5 years of the last prior conviction or release, neither the new felony nor one of the two priors being an s. 893.13 purchase or possession offense, no pardon, and no prior set aside. 782.07.title: Manslaughter; aggravated manslaughter of an elderly person or disabled adult; aggravated manslaughter of a child; aggravated manslaughter of an officer, a firefighter, an emergency medical technician, or a paramedic.

rows.trigger: General manslaughter. Killing of a human being by the act, procurement, or culpable negligence of another, without lawful justification under chapter 776, where the killing is neither excusable homicide nor murder under chapter 782. rows.trigger: Third degree murder: killing without any design to effect death, by a person engaged in the perpetration of or attempt to perpetrate any felony OTHER THAN the nineteen listed in paragraphs (a) through (s). This is an EXCLUSION list, not an inclusion list -- the listed felonies push the conduct up into (1)(a)2. or (3); everything else falls here. Paragraph (l) is a trap for the reader: it excludes distribution of the (1)(a)3.a.-j. substances by a person 18 or older, which is why an adult drug-delivery death is capital and not third degree murder. No dollar value is an element, so min and max are null. Level 8 verified from the F.S. 921.0022(3)(h) chart, entry '782.04(4) / 2nd / Killing of human without design when engaged in act or attempt of any felony other than arson, sexual battery, robbery, burglary, kidnapping, aggravated fleeing or eluding with serious bodily injury or death, aircraft piracy, or unlawfully discharging bomb.'
rows.quote: (4) The unlawful killing of a human being, when perpetrated without any design to effect death, by a person engaged in the perpetration of, or in the attempt to perpetrate, any felony other than any: (a) Trafficking offense prohibited by s. 893.135(1), (b) Arson, (c) Sexual battery, (d) Robbery, (e) Burglary, (f) Kidnapping, (g) Escape, (h) Aggravated child abuse, (i) Aggravated abuse of an elderly person or disabled adult, (j) Aircraft piracy, (k) Unlawful throwing, placing, or discharging of a destructive device or bomb, (l) Unlawful distribution of any substance listed in sub-subparagraphs (1)(a)3.a.-j. by a person 18 years of age or older, when such substance is proven to have caused, or is proven to have been a substantial factor in producing, the death of the user, (m) Carjacking, (n) Home-invasion robbery, (o) Aggravated stalking, (p) Murder of another human being, (q) Aggravated fleeing or eluding with serious bodily injury or death, (r) Resisting an officer with violence to his or her person, or (s) Felony that is an act of terrorism or is in furtherance of an act of terrorism, including a felony under s. 775.30, s. 775.32, s. 775.33, s. 775.34, or s. 775.35, is murder in the third degree and constitutes a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Juvenile fentanyl-delivery murder: killing without any design to effect death resulting from unlawful distribution BY A PERSON LESS THAN 18 YEARS OF AGE of any substance or mixture he or she knew or reasonably should have known contained dangerous fentanyl or fentanyl analogs, proven to have caused or to have been a substantial factor in producing the death of the user. This is the under-18 mirror of (1)(a)3. and carries a scienter element ('knew or reasonably should have known') that (1)(a)3. does not state. It is also narrower in substance: only dangerous fentanyl or fentanyl analogs as defined in (5)(a)1. by reference to s. 893.135(1)(c)4.a.(I)-(VII), not the full a.-j. list. Definitions for this subsection are in (5)(a): 'Dangerous fentanyl or fentanyl analogs' and 'Distribute' (same meaning as s. 893.02). No dollar value and no drug-weight threshold is an element, so min and max are null. Level is null and this is a genuine gap, not an oversight: I searched the entire F.S. 921.0022 chart text for '782.04' and it returns only four entries -- 782.04(1), (2), (3), and (4). Subsection (5) is UNRANKED in the chart. I did not read s. 921.0023, so I am not inferring a default level.
rows.quote: (5)(a) As used in this subsection, the term: 1. "Dangerous fentanyl or fentanyl analogs" means any controlled substance described in s. 893.135(1)(c)4.a.(I)-(VII). 2. "Distribute" has the same meaning as in s. 893.02. (b) The unlawful killing of a human being, when perpetrated without any design to effect death, which resulted from the unlawful distribution by a person less than 18 years of age of any substance or mixture that he or she knew or reasonably should have known contained dangerous fentanyl or fentanyl analogs when such substance or mixture is proven to have caused, or is proven to have been a substantial factor in producing, the death of the user, is murder in the third degree and constitutes a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: CRITICAL FRAMING: this entire section assigns NO degree of offense to anything and contains NO dollar amounts. It is the sentencing-computation statute (scoresheet points and lowest permissible sentence). Degrees come from the substantive offense statutes; severity levels come from s. 921.0022. Every row below therefore has degree 'no degree assigned' and min/max null, and no row here may be read as grading any crime.
rows.quote: 921.0024 Criminal Punishment Code; worksheet computations; scoresheets.

rows.trigger: Total sentence points equal to or less than 44. Prescribes the sanction directly by point score, not by offense degree. Note the discretionary escape hatch in the same sentence: the court may still impose prison up to the statutory maximum.
rows.quote: The lowest permissible sentence is the minimum sentence that may be imposed by the trial court, absent a valid reason for departure. The lowest permissible sentence is any nonstate prison sanction in which the total sentence points equals or is less than 44 points, unless the court determines within its discretion that a prison sentence, which may be up to the statutory maximums for the offenses committed, is appropriate.

rows.trigger: Total sentence points exceed 44. Prescribes a term directly by arithmetic formula: (total points minus 28) reduced by 25 percent, expressed in prison months.
rows.quote: When the total sentence points exceeds 44 points, the lowest permissible sentence in prison months shall be calculated by subtracting 28 points from the total sentence points and decreasing the remaining total by 25 percent.

rows.trigger: Defines the top of the permissible range as the statutory maximum under s. 775.082 for the primary offense and any additional offenses before the court, and authorizes concurrent or consecutive sentences. The maximum is imported from s. 775.082, not assigned here.
rows.quote: The total sentence points shall be calculated only as a means of determining the lowest permissible sentence. The permissible range for sentencing shall be the lowest permissible sentence up to and including the statutory maximum, as defined in s. 775.082, for the primary offense and any additional offenses before the court for sentencing. The sentencing court may impose such sentences concurrently or consecutively.

rows.trigger: Floor on any state prison sentence: it must exceed 1 year. Applies regardless of point score or offense degree.
rows.quote: However, any sentence to state prison must exceed 1 year.

rows.trigger: OVERRIDE PROVISION, easy to miss because it sits mid-paragraph: when the scoresheet's lowest permissible sentence is higher than the statutory maximum for the offense, the code sentence controls and must be imposed. The degree of the offense does not cap exposure in that situation.
rows.quote: If the lowest permissible sentence under the code exceeds the statutory maximum sentence as provided in s. 775.082, the sentence required by the code must be imposed.

rows.trigger: Total sentence points greater than or equal to 363. Authorizes life imprisonment by point score alone, with no degree named and no lower bound tied to the offense's own grading; also strips discretionary early release except executive clemency or conditional medical release.
rows.quote: If the total sentence points are greater than or equal to 363, the court may sentence the offender to life imprisonment. An offender sentenced to life imprisonment under this section is not eligible for any form of discretionary early release, except executive clemency or conditional medical release under s. 947.149.

rows.trigger: The worksheet itself. Primary offense points by offense severity level (level 10 = 116, 9 = 92, 8 = 74, 7 = 56, 6 = 36, 5 = 28, 4 = 22, 3 = 16, 2 = 10, 1 = 4); additional offenses (10 = 58, 9 = 46, 8 = 37, 7 = 28, 6 = 18, 5 = 5.4, 4 = 3.6, 3 = 2.4, 2 = 1.2, 1 = 0.7, M = 0.2 each); victim injury (2nd degree murder-death = 240, death = 120, severe = 40, moderate = 18, slight = 4, sexual penetration = 80, sexual contact = 40 each); prior record (10 = 29, 9 = 23, 8 = 19, 7 = 14, 6 = 9, 5 = 3.6, 4 = 2.4, 3 = 1.6, 2 = 0.8, 1 = 0.5, M = 0.2 each). The levels are inputs taken from s. 921.0022 / s. 921.0023; this paragraph assigns points, not levels and not degrees.
rows.quote: (1)(a) The Criminal Punishment Code worksheet is used to compute the subtotal and total sentence points as follows: FLORIDA CRIMINAL PUNISHMENT CODE WORKSHEET

rows.trigger: Legal status points. Any form of legal status existing at the time of the offense before the court adds 4 points.
rows.quote: WORKSHEET KEY: Legal status points are assessed when any form of legal status existed at the time the offender committed an offense before the court for sentencing. Four (4) sentence points are assessed for an offender's legal status.

rows.trigger: Community sanction violation before the court: 6 points for each violation and each successive violation, subject to the two exceptions in subparagraphs 1. and 2. Read those before relying on the 6-point figure.
rows.quote: Community sanction violation points are assessed when a community sanction violation is before the court for sentencing. Six (6) sentence points are assessed for each community sanction violation and each successive community sanction violation, unless any of the following apply:

rows.trigger: Community sanction violation that includes a new felony conviction before the sentencing court: 12 points instead of 6, for the violation and each successive such violation.
rows.quote: 1. If the community sanction violation includes a new felony conviction before the sentencing court, twelve (12) community sanction violation points are assessed for the violation, and for each successive community sanction violation involving a new felony conviction.

rows.trigger: Violator is a violent felony offender of special concern as defined in s. 948.06, the violation of felony probation or community control does NOT include a new felony conviction (sub-sub I.), and the violation is not based solely on failure to pay costs, fines, or restitution (sub-sub II.): 12 points, per violation and each successive violation. Both conditions I. and II. must be met.
rows.quote: 2. If the community sanction violation is committed by a violent felony offender of special concern as defined in s. 948.06: a. Twelve (12) community sanction violation points are assessed for the violation and for each successive violation of felony probation or community control where: I. The violation does not include a new felony conviction; and II. The community sanction violation is not based solely on the probationer or offender's failure to pay costs or fines or make restitution payments.

rows.trigger: Violent felony offender of special concern whose violation of felony probation or community control DOES include a new felony conviction: 24 points, per violation and each successive violation. Highest community sanction violation assessment in the section.
rows.quote: b. Twenty-four (24) community sanction violation points are assessed for the violation and for each successive violation of felony probation or community control where the violation includes a new felony conviction.

rows.trigger: Anti-stacking rule that closes the community sanction violation key: multiple counts of community sanction violations before the sentencing court cannot multiply the assessment.
rows.quote: Multiple counts of community sanction violations before the sentencing court shall not be a basis for multiplying the assessment of community sanction violation points.

rows.trigger: Prior serious felony: requires BOTH a primary or additional offense ranked level 8, 9, or 10 AND one or more prior serious felonies. Single 30-point assessment (not per prior). A prior serious felony is a level 8, 9, or 10 offense under s. 921.0022 or s. 921.0023 for which the offender is still serving, or whose release date is within 3 years before the date the primary or additional offense was committed.
rows.quote: Prior serious felony points: If the offender has a primary offense or any additional offense ranked in level 8, level 9, or level 10, and one or more prior serious felonies, a single assessment of thirty (30) points shall be added. For purposes of this section, a prior serious felony is an offense in the offender's prior record that is ranked in level 8, level 9, or level 10 under s. 921.0022 or s. 921.0023 and for which the offender is serving a sentence of confinement, supervision, or other sanction or for which the offender's date of release from confinement, supervision, or other sanction, whichever is later, is within 3 years before the date the primary offense or any additional offense was committed.

rows.trigger: Prior capital felony: one or more prior capital felonies adds points equal to TWICE the points received for the primary offense and any additional offense. Includes out-of-jurisdiction felonies that are capital there or would be capital in Florida, and includes pleas of nolo contendere or guilty as well as findings of guilt.
rows.quote: Prior capital felony points: If the offender has one or more prior capital felonies in the offender's criminal record, points shall be added to the subtotal sentence points of the offender equal to twice the number of points the offender receives for the primary offense and any additional offense. A prior capital felony in the offender's criminal record is a previous capital felony offense for which the offender has entered a plea of nolo contendere or guilty or has been found guilty; or a felony in another jurisdiction which is a capital felony in that jurisdiction, or would be a capital felony if the offense were committed in this state.

rows.trigger: Weapon possession points, keyed to the thing possessed: 18 points for possessing a firearm (s. 790.001) while committing or attempting any felony other than those enumerated in s. 775.087(2); 25 points for possessing a semiautomatic firearm (s. 775.087(3)) or a machine gun (s. 790.001) while committing or attempting any felony other than those enumerated in s. 775.087(3). Applies to attempts as well as completed felonies, and to possession without use.
rows.quote: Possession of a firearm, semiautomatic firearm, or machine gun: If the offender is convicted of committing or attempting to commit any felony other than those enumerated in s. 775.087(2) while having in his or her possession: a firearm as defined in s. 790.001, an additional eighteen (18) sentence points are assessed; or if the offender is convicted of committing or attempting to commit any felony other than those enumerated in s. 775.087(3) while having in his or her possession a semiautomatic firearm as defined in s. 775.087(3) or a machine gun as defined in s. 790.001, an additional twenty-five (25) sentence points are assessed.

rows.trigger: Multiplier, aggravated animal cruelty: primary offense under s. 828.12(2) involving knowing and intentional torture or torment that injured, mutilated, or killed the animal multiplies the subtotal by 1.25. Carve-out: 'animal' excludes animals used for agricultural purposes or permitted as captive wildlife under s. 379.303.
rows.quote: Aggravated Animal Cruelty: If the primary offense is aggravated animal cruelty under s. 828.12(2), which included the knowing and intentional torture or torment of an animal that injured, mutilated, or killed the animal, the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 1.25. As used in this paragraph, the term "animal" does not include an animal used for agricultural purposes or permitted as captive wildlife as authorized under s. 379.303.

rows.trigger: Multiplier, drug trafficking: primary offense of trafficking under s. 893.135 ranked level 7 or level 8 multiplies the subtotal by 1.5, but the multiplier is discretionary with the court ('at the discretion of the court'). Substantial assistance under s. 893.135(4) lets the state attorney move to reduce or suspend.
rows.quote: Drug trafficking: If the primary offense is drug trafficking under s. 893.135, the subtotal sentence points are multiplied, at the discretion of the court, for a level 7 or level 8 offense, by 1.5. The state attorney may move the sentencing court to reduce or suspend the sentence of a person convicted of a level 7 or level 8 offense, if the offender provides substantial assistance as described in s. 893.135(4).

rows.trigger: Multiplier, offenses against specified justice system personnel, three separate tiers in one paragraph: 2.5x for s. 775.0823(2), (3), or (4); 2.0x for s. 775.0823(5), (6), (7), (8), or (9); 1.5x for s. 784.07(3), s. 775.0875(1), or s. 775.0823(10) or (11). Stopping at the first sentence of this paragraph would miss the 2.0 and 1.5 tiers.
rows.quote: Violent offenses committed against specified justice system personnel: If the primary offense is a violation of s. 775.0823(2), (3), or (4), the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 2.5. If the primary offense is a violation of s. 775.0823(5), (6), (7), (8), or (9), the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 2.0. If the primary offense is a violation of s. 784.07(3) or s. 775.0875(1), or s. 775.0823(10) or (11), the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 1.5.

rows.trigger: Multiplier, grand theft of a motor vehicle: primary offense must be grand theft of the third degree involving a motor vehicle AND the prior record must contain three or more third-degree grand thefts involving a motor vehicle; subtotal multiplied by 1.5. Degree of the primary offense is imported from the theft statute, not assigned here.
rows.quote: Grand theft of a motor vehicle: If the primary offense is grand theft of the third degree involving a motor vehicle and in the offender's prior record, there are three or more grand thefts of the third degree involving a motor vehicle, the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 1.5.

rows.trigger: Multiplier, fleeing or eluding: primary offense of fleeing or attempting to elude, or aggravated fleeing or eluding, under s. 316.1935, plus one or more prior s. 316.1935 violations in the record; subtotal multiplied by 1.5. Only ONE prior is required here, unlike the three required for the motor vehicle theft multiplier.
rows.quote: Fleeing or attempting to elude a law enforcement officer: If the primary offense is fleeing or attempting to elude a law enforcement officer or aggravated fleeing or eluding in violation of s. 316.1935, and in the offender's prior record, there is one or more violation of s. 316.1935, the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 1.5.

rows.trigger: Multiplier, criminal gang: offense committed for the purpose of benefiting, promoting, or furthering a criminal gang as defined in s. 874.03 multiplies the subtotal by 1.5. Second sentence is a cap that is easy to miss: if the multiplier would push the lowest permissible sentence above the chapter 775 statutory maximum, the court may NOT apply the multiplier and must impose the statutory maximum.
rows.quote: Offense related to a criminal gang: If the offender is convicted of the primary offense and committed that offense for the purpose of benefiting, promoting, or furthering the interests of a criminal gang as defined in s. 874.03, the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 1.5. If applying the multiplier results in the lowest permissible sentence exceeding the statutory maximum sentence for the primary offense under chapter 775, the court may not apply the multiplier and must sentence the defendant to the statutory maximum sentence.

rows.trigger: Multiplier, domestic violence in the presence of a child: primary offense is a crime of domestic violence as defined in s. 741.28, committed in the presence of a child under 16 who is a family or household member (s. 741.28(3)) with the victim or perpetrator; subtotal multiplied by 1.5. No statutory-maximum cap is attached to this multiplier, unlike the gang and adult-on-minor multipliers.
rows.quote: Domestic violence in the presence of a child: If the offender is convicted of the primary offense and the primary offense is a crime of domestic violence, as defined in s. 741.28, which was committed in the presence of a child under 16 years of age who is a family or household member as defined in s. 741.28(3) with the victim or perpetrator, the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 1.5.

rows.trigger: Multiplier, adult-on-minor sex offense: offender 18 or older, victim under 18, primary offense committed on or after October 1, 2014, and the offense is s. 787.01(2) or s. 787.02(2) where the victim was a minor and the defendant committed a sexual battery under ch. 794 or a lewd act under s. 800.04 or s. 847.0135(5) in the course of it; or s. 787.01(3)(a)2. or 3.; or s. 787.02(3)(a)2. or 3.; or s. 794.011 excluding s. 794.011(10); or s. 800.04; or s. 847.0135(5). Subtotal multiplied by 2.0, the largest multiplier in the section. Same statutory-maximum cap as the gang multiplier.
rows.quote: Adult-on-minor sex offense: If the offender was 18 years of age or older and the victim was younger than 18 years of age at the time the offender committed the primary offense, and if the primary offense was an offense committed on or after October 1, 2014, and is a violation of s. 787.01(2) or s. 787.02(2), if the violation involved a victim who was a minor and, in the course of committing that violation, the defendant committed a sexual battery under chapter 794 or a lewd act under s. 800.04 or s. 847.0135(5) against the minor; s. 787.01(3)(a)2. or 3.; s. 787.02(3)(a)2. or 3.; s. 794.011, excluding s. 794.011(10); s. 800.04; or s. 847.0135(5), the subtotal sentence points are multiplied by 2.0. If applying the multiplier results in the lowest permissible sentence exceeding the statutory maximum sentence for the primary offense under chapter 775, the court may not apply the multiplier and must sentence the defendant to the statutory maximum sentence.

rows.trigger: Procedural, read in full and recorded for completeness: one digitized scoresheet per defendant, except separate scoresheets when the felonies were committed under more than one version or revision of the guidelines or code. State attorney prepares; defense counsel reviews for accuracy unless the judge directs otherwise; sentencing judge must approve and sign. No degree and no term assigned.
rows.quote: A single digitized scoresheet shall be prepared for each defendant to determine the permissible range for the sentence that the court may impose, except that if the defendant is before the court for sentencing for more than one felony and the felonies were committed under more than one version or revision of the guidelines or the code, separate digitized scoresheets must be prepared. The scoresheet or scoresheets must cover all the defendant's offenses pending before the court for sentencing. The state attorney shall prepare the digitized scoresheet or scoresheets, which must be presented to the defense counsel for review for accuracy in all cases unless the judge directs otherwise. The defendant's scoresheet or scoresheets must be approved and signed by the sentencing judge.

rows.trigger: Procedural, read in full: Department of Corrections submits the revised digitized scoresheet to the Supreme Court by June 15 each year as necessary and produces approved scoresheets by September 30. Scoresheets must have data cells flagging any mandatory minimum imposed and any downward departure from the lowest permissible sentence. No degree and no term assigned.
rows.quote: The Department of Corrections, in consultation with the Office of the State Courts Administrator, state attorneys, and public defenders, must develop and submit the revised digitized Criminal Punishment Code scoresheet to the Supreme Court for approval by June 15 of each year, as necessary. The digitized scoresheet shall have individual, structured data cells for each data field on the scoresheet. Upon the Supreme Court's approval of the revised digitized scoresheet, the Department of Corrections shall produce and provide the revised digitized scoresheets by September 30 of each year, as necessary. Digitized scoresheets must include individual data cells to indicate whether any prison sentence imposed includes a mandatory minimum sentence or the sentence imposed was a downward departure from the lowest permissible sentence under the Criminal Punishment Code.

rows.trigger: Procedural, read in full: DOC availability of digitized scoresheets to preparers. No degree and no term assigned.
rows.quote: The Department of Corrections shall make available the digitized Criminal Punishment Code scoresheets to those persons charged with the responsibility for preparing scoresheets.

rows.trigger: Procedural, read in full: clerk of the circuit court transmits a complete and accurate digitized copy of each scoresheet to DOC, at least monthly by the first of each month, and may send them collectively. No degree and no term assigned.
rows.quote: The clerk of the circuit court shall transmit a complete and accurate digitized copy of the Criminal Punishment Code scoresheet used in each sentencing proceeding to the Department of Corrections. Scoresheets must be electronically transmitted no less frequently than monthly, by the first of each month, and may be sent collectively.

rows.trigger: Procedural, read in full: a digitized sentencing scoresheet must be prepared for EVERY defendant sentenced for a felony offense, and it plus attachments prepared under Fla. R. Crim. P. 3.701, 3.702, 3.703 or any other applicable rule must accompany the uniform judgment and sentence form sent to DOC. No degree and no term assigned.
rows.quote: A digitized sentencing scoresheet must be prepared for every defendant who is sentenced for a felony offense. The individual offender's digitized Criminal Punishment Code scoresheet and any attachments thereto prepared pursuant to Rule 3.701, Rule 3.702, or Rule 3.703, Florida Rules of Criminal Procedure, or any other rule pertaining to the preparation and submission of felony sentencing scoresheets, must be included with the uniform judgment and sentence form provided to the Department of Corrections.

rows.trigger: Offender 18 years of age or older; victim less than 12 years of age; either a completed sexual battery OR an attempt in which the offender injures the victim's sexual organs. No dollar amount appears anywhere in this section, so min and max are null throughout: value is never the trigger. Level is null because this offense does not appear in the s. 921.0022 ranking chart (the chart's 794.011(2) entries are the 1st-degree attempt entry and the life-felony entry, both level 9); do not assume a level for a capital felony. Procedure: s. 921.1425 governs death-vs-life; prosecutor must file notice of intent to seek death within 45 days after arraignment.
rows.quote: A person 18 years of age or older who commits sexual battery upon, or in an attempt to commit sexual battery injures the sexual organs of, a person less than 12 years of age commits a capital felony, punishable as provided in ss. 775.082 and 921.1425. In all capital cases under this section, the procedure set forth in s. 921.1425 shall be followed in order to determine a sentence of death or life imprisonment. If the prosecutor intends to seek the death penalty, the prosecutor must give notice to the defendant and file the notice with the court within 45 days after arraignment. The notice must contain a list of the aggravating factors the state intends to prove and has reason to believe it can prove beyond a reasonable doubt. A $0 case is a third degree felony.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses, or possesses with intent to fraudulently use, personal identification information concerning another person without first obtaining that person’s consent, commits the offense of fraudulent use of personal identification information, which is a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: $5,000 or more, OR -- as a fully INDEPENDENT ALTERNATIVE -- fraudulent use of the personal identification information of 10 or more but fewer than 20 persons. The count prong has NO dollar component whatsoever: 10 victims with zero pecuniary benefit is still a second degree felony. Note also that the statute's own text states no upper dollar bound for this paragraph; the 50000 exclusive ceiling recorded here is supplied only by the $50,000 threshold in (2)(c), not by the words of (2)(b). rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a person without first obtaining that person’s consent commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $5,000 or more or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 10 or more persons, but fewer than 20 persons, without their consent.

rows.trigger: TRAILING SENTENCE INSIDE PARAGRAPH (2)(b) THAT PRESCRIBES A TERM DIRECTLY WITHOUT NAMING A DEGREE. Every conviction under (2)(b) -- including one resting purely on the 10-to-19-victim count prong with no dollar loss -- carries a 3-year MANDATORY MINIMUM prison sentence. Anyone who reads only the degree sentence of (2)(b) and stops will understate this exposure as an ordinary probationable second degree felony.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of committing the offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 3 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: $50,000 or more, with NO UPPER BOUND -- max is null because this paragraph is the top of the value ladder and reaches any amount however large. Alternatively and independently, fraudulent use of the personal identification information of 20 or more but fewer than 30 persons, with no dollar element. Not found in the s. 921.0022 ranking chart, so level is null rather than guessed.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a person without first obtaining that person’s consent commits a felony of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $50,000 or more or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 20 or more persons, but fewer than 30 persons, without their consent.

rows.trigger: Prescribes a term directly without naming a degree. Every conviction under (2)(c) carries a 5-year MANDATORY MINIMUM, including one resting solely on the 20-to-29-victim count prong with no dollar loss.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of committing the offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 5 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: THIS IS THE PROVISION MOST LIKELY TO BE MISSED IN THIS ENTIRE SECTION. A SECOND, HIGHER, SEPARATELY NUMBERED-BY-NOTHING THRESHOLD BURIED IN THE LAST SENTENCE OF PARAGRAPH (2)(c): $100,000 or more, with NO UPPER BOUND, or 30 or more persons with NO UPPER BOUND on victim count, raises the mandatory minimum from 5 years to 10 years. The degree remains first degree felony -- this sentence names no degree, it prescribes a term -- so a reader tracking only degrees will record the $50,000 tier and stop, exactly as happened in the F.S. 812.014(2)(b) failure. The 30-or-more-persons prong is again independent of any dollar amount.
rows.quote: If the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $100,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 30 or more persons without their consent, notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of committing the offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: Assigns no degree but governs how the (2)(b) and (2)(c) mandatory minimums interact with the Criminal Punishment Code. Recorded because it defeats the natural assumption that a scoresheet or a statutory maximum caps the mandatory minimum: THE MANDATORY MINIMUM MUST BE IMPOSED EVEN IF IT EXCEEDS THE MAXIMUM otherwise authorized under s. 775.082, s. 775.084, or chapter 921. It also expressly preserves the court's power to go higher.
rows.quote: Neither paragraph (2)(b) nor paragraph (2)(c) prevents a court from imposing a greater sentence of incarceration as authorized by law. If the minimum mandatory terms of imprisonment imposed under paragraph (2)(b) or paragraph (2)(c) exceed the maximum sentences authorized under s. 775.082, s. 775.084, or the Criminal Punishment Code under chapter 921, the mandatory minimum sentence must be imposed. If the mandatory minimum terms of imprisonment under paragraph (2)(b) or paragraph (2)(c) are less than the sentence that could be imposed under s. 775.082, s. 775.084, or the Criminal Punishment Code under chapter 921, the sentence imposed by the court must include the mandatory minimum term of imprisonment as required by paragraph (2)(b) or paragraph (2)(c).

rows.trigger: Harassment purpose, not fraud purpose. Value is irrelevant; min and max are null because no dollar amount is an element. Reaches POSSESSES, USES, OR ATTEMPTS TO USE -- an attempt alone completes the offense. "Harass" is narrowed by the definition in (1)(c), which excludes accepted commercial purposes and constitutionally protected conduct such as organized protests. Note this is the only base offense in the section that is a misdemeanor, and subsections (5)(a) and (10)(a) can each convert it to a third degree felony.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization possesses, uses, or attempts to use personal identification information concerning a person without first obtaining that person’s consent, and who does so for the purpose of harassing that person, commits the offense of harassment by use of personal identification information, which is a misdemeanor of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082 or s. 775.083.

rows.trigger: RECLASSIFICATION, NOT A STANDALONE OFFENSE. Applies when ANY offense prohibited under this section was facilitated or furthered by use of a public record as defined in s. 119.011. Converts the (4) harassment first degree misdemeanor into a third degree felony. Level 2 is taken from the express ranking sentence at the end of subsection (5), not from the s. 921.0022 chart. Scope is not one of dwelling/item/prior -- none of those categories exist in this statute -- so it is recorded as the narrowing circumstance itself.
rows.quote: If an offense prohibited under this section was facilitated or furthered by the use of a public record, as defined in s. 119.011, the offense is reclassified to the next higher degree as follows: (a) A misdemeanor of the first degree is reclassified as a felony of the third degree.

rows.trigger: Reclassification. Any third degree felony under this section -- (2)(a), (8)(a), or (9) -- becomes a second degree felony when facilitated or furthered by use of a public record. Level is null because the reclassified rank is defined as one level above the base offense's s. 921.0022 ranking, and the three possible base offenses do not share a single ranking ((2)(a) is level 4; (8)(a) and (9) are unranked in the chart).
rows.quote: (b) A felony of the third degree is reclassified as a felony of the second degree. ... For purposes of sentencing under chapter 921 and incentive gain-time eligibility under chapter 944, a felony offense that is reclassified under this subsection is ranked one level above the ranking under s. 921.0022 of the felony offense committed, and a misdemeanor offense that is reclassified under this subsection is ranked in level 2 of the offense severity ranking chart in s. 921.0022.

rows.trigger: Reclassification. Any second degree felony under this section -- (2)(b), (6), (7), (8)(b), or (11) -- becomes a first degree felony when facilitated or furthered by use of a public record. NOTE THE GAP: subsection (5) provides no reclassification for an offense that is already a first degree felony ((2)(c) or (8)(c)); the ladder in (5) stops at (c), unlike subsection (10) which continues to a life felony.
rows.quote: (c) A felony of the second degree is reclassified as a felony of the first degree.

rows.trigger: VICTIM-STATUS OFFENSE WITH NO DOLLAR ELEMENT AT ALL. min and max are null and that is critical: a single fraudulent use of the personal identification information of a person under 18, or of a person 60 or older, is a SECOND DEGREE FELONY regardless of amount -- a $1 case carries the same degree as a $5,000 case under (2)(b), and jumps three severity levels above the (2)(a) base. The s. 921.0022 chart entry for this subsection describes only the under-18 branch, but the statutory text plainly also covers individuals 60 years of age or older; level 8 is recorded from that chart entry.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning an individual who is younger than 18 years of age or 60 years of age or older without first obtaining the consent of that individual or of his or her legal guardian commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: No dollar element. Aggravated by the defendant's custodial relationship to a victim under 18 or 60 or older: parent, legal guardian, or anyone otherwise exercising custodial authority. Note the mens rea here omits "without authorization" and omits any lack-of-consent element -- it requires only willful and fraudulent use. Ranked level 9, one level above (6), the highest ranking of any offense in this section. The s. 921.0022 chart annotates this entry "2nd,PBL"; I did not read the chart's legend, so I record the annotation without interpreting it, and the degree stated in the statutory text itself is a felony of the second degree.
rows.quote: Any person who is in the relationship of parent or legal guardian, or who otherwise exercises custodial authority over an individual who is younger than 18 years of age or 60 years of age or older, who willfully and fraudulently uses personal identification information of that individual commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: NO DOLLAR FLOOR. Parallel base offense for the personal identification information of a DECEASED INDIVIDUAL OR A DISSOLVED BUSINESS ENTITY -- note that (1)(d) defines "individual" to exclude corporations and partnerships, so this subsection is the only route to entity victims. Reaches possession with intent to fraudulently use, so no completed use and no loss is required. No consent element, since there is no one to consent. Not in the s. 921.0022 chart, so level is null.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and fraudulently uses, or possesses with intent to fraudulently use, personal identification information concerning a deceased individual or dissolved business entity commits the offense of fraudulent use or possession with intent to use personal identification information of a deceased individual or dissolved business entity, a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: $5,000 or more, OR -- independently, with no dollar element -- 10 or more but fewer than 20 deceased individuals or dissolved business entities. As with (2)(b), the paragraph's own text states no upper dollar bound; the 50000 exclusive ceiling comes only from (8)(c). Requires actual fraudulent use, not possession.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a deceased individual or dissolved business entity commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of injury or fraud perpetrated is $5,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 10 or more but fewer than 20 deceased individuals or dissolved business entities.

rows.trigger: Trailing sentence prescribing a term without naming a degree: 3-year MANDATORY MINIMUM on every (8)(b) conviction, including one resting solely on the 10-to-19-entity count prong with no dollar loss.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of committing the offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 3 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: $50,000 or more with NO UPPER BOUND, or independently 20 or more but fewer than 30 deceased individuals or dissolved business entities. Named offense: aggravated fraudulent use of the personal identification information of multiple deceased individuals or dissolved business entities. Not in the s. 921.0022 chart, so level is null.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning a deceased individual or dissolved business entity commits the offense of aggravated fraudulent use of the personal identification information of multiple deceased individuals or dissolved business entities, a felony of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of injury or fraud perpetrated is $50,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 20 or more but fewer than 30 deceased individuals or dissolved business entities.

rows.trigger: Prescribes a term without naming a degree: 5-year mandatory minimum on every (8)(c) conviction. The statute says "minimum mandatory" here where the parallel (2)(c) says "mandatory minimum"; the wording differs but is recorded verbatim.
rows.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of the offense described in this paragraph to a minimum mandatory sentence of 5 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: SECOND HIDDEN THRESHOLD IN THE LAST SENTENCE OF (8)(c), the deceased-victim twin of the (2)(c) trap. $100,000 or more, or 30 or more deceased individuals or dissolved business entities, both with NO UPPER BOUND, raises the mandatory minimum to 10 years. No degree is named; the degree remains first degree felony under (8)(c). Stopping at the $50,000 sentence of this paragraph understates exposure by five years of mandatory time.
rows.quote: If the pecuniary benefit, the value of the services received, the payment sought to be avoided, or the amount of the injury or fraud perpetrated is $100,000 or more, or if the person fraudulently uses the personal identification information of 30 or more deceased individuals or dissolved business entities, notwithstanding any other provision of law, the court shall sentence any person convicted of an offense described in this paragraph to a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years’ imprisonment.

rows.trigger: NO DOLLAR ELEMENT AND NO REAL VICTIM REQUIRED. Reaches counterfeit or fictitious personal identification information concerning a FICTITIOUS PERSON as well as a real person -- so-called synthetic identity conduct is a third degree felony even though no actual human is harmed. Reaches CREATES or USES or POSSESSES WITH INTENT TO USE. "Counterfeit or fictitious personal identification information" is defined in (1)(g) by a reasonably-prudent-person standard. Requires intent to commit or facilitate a fraud on another person. Not in the s. 921.0022 chart, so level is null.
rows.quote: Any person who willfully and fraudulently creates or uses, or possesses with intent to fraudulently use, counterfeit or fictitious personal identification information concerning a fictitious person, or concerning a real person without first obtaining that real person’s consent, with intent to use such counterfeit or fictitious personal identification information for the purpose of committing or facilitating the commission of a fraud on another person, commits the offense of fraudulent creation or use, or possession with intent to fraudulently use, counterfeit or fictitious personal identification information, a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: RECLASSIFICATION, NOT A STANDALONE OFFENSE. Triggered when the defendant, for the purpose of obtaining or using personal identification information, misrepresents himself or herself as a law enforcement officer; an employee or representative of a bank, credit card company, credit counseling company, or credit reporting agency; or wrongfully represents that he or she is seeking to help the victim with a credit-history problem. Converts the (4) misdemeanor into a third degree felony. Level 2 is taken from the express ranking sentence at the end of subsection (10).
rows.quote: Any person who commits an offense described in this section and for the purpose of obtaining or using personal identification information misrepresents himself or herself to be a law enforcement officer; an employee or representative of a bank, credit card company, credit counseling company, or credit reporting agency; or any person who wrongfully represents that he or she is seeking to assist the victim with a problem with the victim’s credit history shall have the offense reclassified as follows: (a) In the case of a misdemeanor, the offense is reclassified as a felony of the third degree.

rows.trigger: Reclassification of any third degree felony under this section to a second degree felony on the impersonation trigger. Level null: the statute ranks it one level above the base offense's s. 921.0022 or s. 921.0023 ranking, and the possible base offenses ((2)(a) level 4; (8)(a) and (9) unranked) do not share one ranking.
rows.quote: (b) In the case of a felony of the third degree, the offense is reclassified as a felony of the second degree. ... For purposes of sentencing under chapter 921, a felony offense that is reclassified under this subsection is ranked one level above the ranking under s. 921.0022 or s. 921.0023 of the felony offense committed, and a misdemeanor offense that is reclassified under this subsection is ranked in level 2 of the offense severity ranking chart.

rows.trigger: Reclassification of any second degree felony under this section -- (2)(b), (6), (7), (8)(b), or (11) -- to a first degree felony on the impersonation trigger.
rows.quote: (c) In the case of a felony of the second degree, the offense is reclassified as a felony of the first degree.

rows.trigger: THE SINGLE HIGHEST EXPOSURE IN THIS SECTION AND THE LAST SUBPARAGRAPH OF THE PARAGRAPH -- exactly the position where a reader who found the answer at (a), (b), or (c) stops. A first degree felony under this section, or a first degree felony punishable by life, becomes a LIFE FELONY when the impersonation trigger applies. So a (2)(c) or (8)(c) case in which the defendant posed as a bank representative or a police officer is not a 30-year first degree felony but a life felony. Subsection (5) has no equivalent top rung; only (10) reaches this degree.
rows.quote: (d) In the case of a felony of the first degree or a felony of the first degree punishable by a term of imprisonment not exceeding life, the offense is reclassified as a life felony.

rows.trigger: NO DOLLAR ELEMENT WHATSOEVER -- a single unauthorized fraudulent use of one protected person's information is a second degree felony no matter how small the amount. The protected classes are broad and largely non-obvious: an individual 60 or older; a disabled adult as defined in s. 825.101; a public servant as defined in s. 838.014; a veteran as defined in s. 1.01; a first responder as defined in s. 125.01045; any individual employed by the State of Florida; and any individual employed by the Federal Government. The 60-or-older branch overlaps subsection (6). Not in the s. 921.0022 chart, so level is null. I did not read the four incorporated definitions, so the outer boundary of each class is unverified.
rows.quote: A person who willfully and without authorization fraudulently uses personal identification information concerning an individual who is 60 years of age or older; a disabled adult as defined in s. 825.101; a public servant as defined in s. 838.014; a veteran as defined in s. 1.01; a first responder as defined in s. 125.01045; an individual who is employed by the State of Florida; or an individual who is employed by the Federal Government without first obtaining the consent of that individual commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Assigns no degree but imposes a monetary consequence on EVERY conviction under this section, including a withhold of adjudication and including a plea of nolo contendere: a mandatory $1,001 surcharge that THE COURT MAY NOT WAIVE, on top of any fine under s. 775.083 and any restitution under s. 775.089. Recorded because it attaches to every row above, including the (4) misdemeanor.
rows.quote: In addition to any sanction imposed when a person pleads guilty or nolo contendere to, or is found guilty of, regardless of adjudication, a violation of this section, the court shall impose a surcharge of $1,001. ... (d) The surcharge may not be waived by the court. In the event that the person has been ordered to pay restitution in accordance with s. 775.089, the surcharge shall be included in a judgment.

rows.trigger: Assigns no degree. Statute of limitations, recorded because it is a limit on exposure rather than a source of it, and because its reach is partial in a way easily misread: the 3-year period with the discovery extension applies ONLY to prosecutions under subsection (2), subsection (6), or subsection (7). Subsections (8), (9), (10), and (11) are NOT named in this subsection, so their limitation periods come from elsewhere in the law and are not established by this section. Ambiguity noted rather than resolved -- I did not read the general limitations statute.
rows.quote: A prosecution of an offense prohibited under subsection (2), subsection (6), or subsection (7) must be commenced within 3 years after the offense occurred. However, a prosecution may be commenced within 1 year after discovery of the offense by an aggrieved party, or by a person who has a legal duty to represent the aggrieved party and who is not a party to the offense, if such prosecution is commenced within 5 years after the violation occurred.

fs-316-193-2025.title: Driving under the influence; penalties.

rows.trigger: Defines the offense only. Assigns NO degree and NO term of its own; it routes all punishment to subsection (2), which is itself subject to the exceptions in (2)(b), (3), and (4). Reading (1) alone tells a reader nothing about exposure. NOTE: no provision anywhere in 316.193 is graded by a dollar amount, so min/max are null on every row in this table; every dollar figure that appears is a fine (a penalty), never a grading trigger.
rows.quote: A person is guilty of the offense of driving under the influence and is subject to punishment as provided in subsection (2) if the person is driving or in actual physical control of a vehicle within this state and:(a) The person is under the influence of alcoholic beverages, any chemical substance set forth in s. 877.111, or any substance controlled under chapter 893, when affected to the extent that the person’s normal faculties are impaired;(b) The person has a blood-alcohol level of 0.08 or more grams of alcohol per 100 milliliters of blood; or (c) The person has a breath-alcohol level of 0.08 or more grams of alcohol per 210 liters of breath.

rows.trigger: First conviction. Fine range is the penalty, not a grading trigger. The whole of (2)(a) applies only 'Except as provided in paragraph (b), subsection (3), or subsection (4)' -- a reader who stops at (2)(a) will miss the felony provisions entirely.
rows.quote: Except as provided in paragraph (b), subsection (3), or subsection (4), any person who is convicted of a violation of subsection (1) shall be punished:1. By a fine of:a. Not less than $500 or more than $1,000 for a first conviction.

rows.trigger: Second conviction, with no time limit stated on how old the prior is. Fine range is the penalty, not a grading trigger.
rows.quote: b. Not less than $1,000 or more than $2,000 for a second conviction; and

rows.trigger: First conviction. The statute prescribes a term directly and names no degree. A 6-month maximum corresponds to a second degree misdemeanor under s. 775.082, but s. 316.193 itself does not say so and this row does not infer it.
rows.quote: 2. By imprisonment for:a. Not more than 6 months for a first conviction.

rows.trigger: Second conviction. Term prescribed directly, no degree named. A 9-month maximum matches no standard misdemeanor term in s. 775.082; the statute is silent on degree and this row records only what it says.
rows.quote: b. Not more than 9 months for a second conviction.

rows.trigger: Second conviction. Mandatory ignition interlock for at least 1 year, contingent on the person qualifying for a permanent or restricted license. Not a degree provision but a mandatory consequence attached to a second conviction.
rows.quote: 3. For a second conviction, by mandatory placement for a period of at least 1 year, at the convicted person’s sole expense, of an ignition interlock device approved by the department in accordance with s. 316.1938 upon all vehicles that are individually or jointly leased or owned and routinely operated by the convicted person, when the convicted person qualifies for a permanent or restricted license.

rows.trigger: Third violation where the offense occurs WITHIN 10 years after a prior conviction. Level 3 verified from the F.S. 921.0022(3)(c) LEVEL 3 chart, entry '316.193(2)(b), 3rd, Felony DUI, 3rd conviction.' Also carries mandatory interlock of not less than 2 years.
rows.quote: Any person who is convicted of a third violation of this section for an offense that occurs within 10 years after a prior conviction for a violation of this section commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084. In addition, the court shall order the mandatory placement for a period of not less than 2 years, at the convicted person’s sole expense, of an ignition interlock device approved by the department in accordance with s. 316.1938 upon all vehicles that are individually or jointly leased or owned and routinely operated by the convicted person, when the convicted person qualifies for a permanent or restricted license.

rows.trigger: THIS IS THE STOP-READING TRAP IN THIS SECTION. A third violation occurring MORE THAN 10 years after the prior conviction is NOT a felony. The statute prescribes a fine of $2,000 to $5,000 and imprisonment of not more than 12 months and names no degree at all. Anyone who opens (2)(b), reads subparagraph 1, and concludes 'third DUI = third degree felony' states the law wrongly for every defendant whose prior is older than 10 years. Mandatory interlock of at least 2 years still applies.
rows.quote: Any person who is convicted of a third violation of this section for an offense that occurs more than 10 years after the date of a prior conviction for a violation of this section shall be punished by a fine of not less than $2,000 or more than $5,000 and by imprisonment for not more than 12 months. The portion of a fine imposed in excess of $2,500 pursuant to this subparagraph shall be remitted by the clerk to the Department of Revenue for deposit into the General Revenue Fund. In addition, the court shall order the mandatory placement for a period of at least 2 years, at the convicted person’s sole expense, of an ignition interlock device approved by the department in accordance with s. 316.1938 upon all vehicles that are individually or jointly leased or owned and routinely operated by the convicted person, when the convicted person qualifies for a permanent or restricted license.

rows.trigger: Fourth or subsequent violation, REGARDLESS of when any prior conviction occurred -- the 10-year window in subparagraphs 1 and 2 does not apply here. Same degree as (2)(b)1 but ranked twice as severe: Level 6 verified from the F.S. 921.0022(3)(f) LEVEL 6 chart, entry '316.193(2)(b), 3rd, Felony DUI, 4th or subsequent conviction.' Fine floor is stated permissively ('may be not less than $2,000'), which is ambiguous on its face as to whether the $2,000 floor is mandatory.
rows.quote: Any person who is convicted of a fourth or subsequent violation of this section, regardless of when any prior conviction for a violation of this section occurred, commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084. However, the fine imposed for such fourth or subsequent violation may be not less than $2,000. The portion of a fine imposed in excess of $1,000 pursuant to this subparagraph shall be remitted by the clerk to the Department of Revenue for deposit into the General Revenue Fund.

rows.trigger: Discretionary ('may order') interlock of at least 6 continuous months where the person's blood- or breath-alcohol level was .08 or higher at the time of the offense. Note this sets no minimum number of prior convictions, so it can reach a first offense.
rows.quote: In addition to the penalties in paragraph (a), the court may order placement, at the convicted person’s sole expense, of an ignition interlock device approved by the department in accordance with s. 316.1938 for at least 6 continuous months upon all vehicles that are individually or jointly leased or owned and routinely operated by the convicted person if, at the time of the offense, the person had a blood-alcohol level or breath-alcohol level of .08 or higher.

rows.trigger: Requires all three of (3)(a) violation of subsection (1), (3)(b) operating a vehicle, and (3)(c) causing or contributing to causing damage to the property OR the person of another. Note 'contributes to causing' -- sole causation is not required. Not ranked in the F.S. 921.0022 chart, which covers felonies only.
rows.quote: Any person:(a) Who is in violation of subsection (1);(b) Who operates a vehicle; and (c) Who, by reason of such operation, causes or contributes to causing:1. Damage to the property or person of another commits a misdemeanor of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082 or s. 775.083.

rows.trigger: Causes or contributes to causing serious bodily injury to another, as that term is defined in s. 316.1933. No prior conviction required -- a first-time offender falls here. Level 7 verified from the F.S. 921.0022(3)(g) LEVEL 7 chart, entry '316.193(3)(c)2., 3rd, DUI resulting in serious bodily injury.'
rows.quote: Serious bodily injury to another, as defined in s. 316.1933, commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: Causes or contributes to causing the death of any human being OR unborn child ('unborn child' has the meaning in s. 775.021(5)). No prior conviction required. Level 8 verified from the F.S. 921.0022(3)(h) LEVEL 8 chart, entry '316.193(3)(c)3.a., 2nd, DUI manslaughter.' Subject to the 4-year mandatory minimum in the flush language at the end of subsection (3).
rows.quote: The death of any human being or unborn child commits DUI manslaughter, and commits:a. A felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.

rows.trigger: DUI manslaughter elevated one degree where BOTH conditions are met: the person knew or should have known the crash occurred, AND the person failed to give information and render aid under s. 316.062. Both (I) and (II) are required -- they are joined by 'and'. Level 9 verified from the F.S. 921.0022(3)(i) LEVEL 9 chart, entry '316.193(3)(c)3.b., 1st, DUI manslaughter; failing to render aid or give information.'
rows.quote: b. A felony of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if:(I) At the time of the crash, the person knew, or should have known, that the crash occurred; and (II) The person failed to give information and render aid as required by s. 316.062.

rows.trigger: DUI manslaughter elevated one degree by criminal history: a prior conviction under this same subparagraph (DUI manslaughter), or under s. 327.35(3)(a)3.c. (BUI manslaughter), s. 782.071 (vehicular homicide), or s. 782.072 (vessel homicide). Level 9 verified from the F.S. 921.0022(3)(i) LEVEL 9 chart. The statute text carries an editor's footnote: the citation was substituted for a reference to s. 327.35(3)(c)3. to conform to a 2025 redesignation.
rows.quote: c. A felony of the first degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084, if the person has a prior conviction under this subparagraph, 1s. 327.35(3)(a)3.c., s. 782.071, or s. 782.072.

rows.trigger: Unnumbered flush paragraph closing subsection (3). Easy to miss because it sits after the last subparagraph and carries no cite of its own. It imposes a 4-year mandatory minimum on EVERY DUI manslaughter conviction, i.e. on 3.a., 3.b., and 3.c. alike, and supplies the definition of 'unborn child'.
rows.quote: For purposes of this subsection, the term “unborn child” has the same meaning as provided in s. 775.021(5). A person who is convicted of DUI manslaughter shall be sentenced to a mandatory minimum term of imprisonment of 4 years.

rows.trigger: CONCLUDING FLUSH LANGUAGE of paragraph (1)(a), easily missed because it sits below subparagraph 3. rows.quote: For the purpose of this paragraph, a plant, including, but not limited to, a seedling or cutting, is a “cannabis plant” if it has some readily observable evidence of root formation, such as root hairs. To determine if a piece or part of a cannabis plant severed from the cannabis plant is itself a cannabis plant, the severed piece or part must have some readily observable evidence of root formation, such as root hairs. Callous tissue is not readily observable evidence of root formation. The viability and sex of a plant and the fact that the plant may or may not be a dead harvested plant are not relevant in determining if the plant is a “cannabis plant” or in the charging of an offense under this paragraph. Upon conviction, the court shall impose the longest term of imprisonment provided for in this paragraph.

Separate convictions and sentences for the conspiracy and the completed offense are expressly permitted. No weight threshold of its own.
